source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives minimax rates for Hölder-smooth pointwise CATE estimation, using localized fuzzy hypotheses and a local-polynomial R-learner.
The paper studies conditional-independence testing under smooth conditional laws and gives binned-test critical-radius bounds in total variation.
The publication develops two nonparametric treatment-effect-heterogeneity tests, including a constant conditional-average-treatment-effect null.

source_verification_receipts.version: JASA accepted author version, online 18 May 2026
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The publisher lists the cited treatment-effect-homogeneity paper as an accepted JASA article.
The paper targets CATE variance and states asymptotic normality and type-I-error control for its intra-fold split statistic.
The article proposes an observational treatment-effect-heterogeneity test based on propensity-reweighted multisample U-statistics and establishes asymptotic normality.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Dai, Shen, and Stern (2023) to related work and state the exact distinction: finite-sample Hölder minimax radius with primitive nuisance smoothness versus their asymptotic propensity-reweighted U-test.

Replace the circular rSharp reference with an explicit finite optimization or finite candidate-rate family before asking the converse to achieve c_sep rSharp; then make the complete-frontier OEQ select and prove the correct member.
Add a strict comparison corollary showing a regime in which the proposed primitive-class guarantee applies while the direct asymptotic homogeneity comparators' assumptions or guarantee do not.

recommended_next_step: Revise the rate-object specification and direct-homogeneity literature comparison, then continue this angle.
